_doc: DIAGNOSTIC ground truth for the Stage 02 book-boundary crop (2026-08-19). Axis-aligned bounds of the BOOK CONTENT — the two visible facing pages, including their coloured headers and side strips — in original Stage 01 anchor pixels. Convention: the fanned block of CLOSED pages beside the spread is deliberately EXCLUDED (it carries no content to lose), and so is the photographer/room. This file grades ONE thing: whether the emitted crop clips page content, for which the bar is ZERO labelled pixels outside the crop. PALESET ADDENDUM 2026-08-28: paleset_01/paleset_02 are the two real phone captures the book detector fails on (book on a pale surface); they are the first labelled pale-background lighting setup here and take the labelled corpus from 6 spreads to 8. Same convention and same independent provenance: hand-read off the committed full-resolution JPEG with 50/100-px ruler overlays at 1:1 and 1.4-1.6x zoom on each edge, then re-checked by drawing the box back onto the frame. paleset_01 is a lap capture, so the book is rotated in frame and its bottom-left corner reaches x=0 while its top-left corner is near x=300 - the axis-aligned box is correspondingly generous on the left, by construction, not by sloppiness. Both labels were read BEFORE any fix was attempted, and they agree with the throwaway background-first probe of 2026-08-28 to within 2 points of frame area (0.577 vs 0.561, 0.436 vs 0.438), which is corroboration, not fitting. PRECISION HAZARD, measured 2026-08-28, and it applies to EVERY row here, not just the new ones: the clipping metric divides by the labelled box area, so a hand-label read to +-20 px is knife-edge against a bar of exactly 0.0 %. On paleset_01 one pixel off the left or right edge costs 0.033 % and one off the top or bottom costs 0.042 %; on paleset_02, 0.036 % and 0.052 %. A 20-px inset all round therefore reports ~3 % and prints as PAGE CONTENT LOST. The six older rows never hit this only because their emitted crops are larger than the label (or the detector abstains and emits the whole frame). paleset_01 is the sharpest case: the book runs OFF the left edge of that frame - the page reaches x=0 in a band around y=2620-2660 - so its label starts at x=0 and ANY crop that starts further right clips it (25 px in = 1.4 %). That is a real property of the capture, not a labelling slip, and it was deliberately not softened by inventing an inset. So: before calling a sub-2 % clip on a paleset row a regression, check WHERE it falls - if the clipped band is blank outer margin with no ink, it is label precision, and the finding is the number plus that adjudication, written down. A clip that removes ink is a real failure at any size. It is NOT a detector accuracy target — do not fit a book detector to these boxes; the load-bearing metric stays testset/gt/gutter.json. Provenance: hand-read off the full-resolution anchor at ~3.7x downscale with a 100-px x/y ruler overlay, independent of every quantity book_boundary.py computes. Append-only per testset/README.md.
_fields: x0,y0,x1,y1 = inclusive-exclusive pixel bounds; anchor names the image (under testset/) the label was read on, except de_01/de_02 which read from gitignored jobs/orient_fix_de* via tools/split_eval ANCHOR_OVERRIDE.
